basis: Atrial conduction dysfunction and chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction define the syndrome; both occur in 17/17 patients.
Primary cervical carcinoma; the uterine cervix is outside the 13 axes.
Hepatitis C infection directly affects the liver; extrahepatic diseases are not assumed.
Premature fusion of metopic and sagittal cranial sutures; neurologic injury is not inherent to nonsyndromic craniosynostosis.
A pancreatic epithelial cyst is a structural pancreatic lesion; endocrine dysfunction and immune disease are not established.
Bilateral congenital absence or hypoplasia of central digits and metacarpals; explicitly nonsyndromic with normal development.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and developmental delay define the phenotype; skeletal polydactyly occurs in 8/8. Renal dysplasia is only occasional.
Motor neuropathy with connective-tissue manifestations: foot/joint abnormalities ~33-67%, aortic dissection 1/3 and bronchiectasis 1/3; estimates come from small series.
Severe inherited demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; weakness and amyotrophy reflect denervation. Supplied scoliosis frequency is based on one patient.
Peripheral neuropathy defines this concept; paraproteinemia is the underlying condition, and an immune mechanism is not universal.
Persistent gastric gland atrophy damages the stomach; the concept does not specify autoimmune or infectious etiology.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain malformations, profound developmental impairment and structural eye anomalies.
Absent calvarium and scalp define the defect. HPO reports cerebellar hypoplasia 80-99% and neuronal migration defects 30-79%, despite usual CNS preservation in the definition.
Louse-transmitted systemic bacterial infection; fever, rash and organ enlargement do not alone establish substantial organ damage.
Multiple cartilage-capped bone tumors with common skeletal deformity and restricted joint movement; neurologic compression is a minority complication.
Neurocutaneous syndrome defined by epidermal nevi and developmental or epileptic abnormalities; ocular abnormalities are only reported without qualifying frequency.
Hepatic fat accumulation with hepatocyte injury and inflammation; associated obesity and diabetes are separate diagnoses.
Developmental impairment is the predominant shared feature of constitutional 5q deletion syndromes; other organ defects depend on the interval. Del(5q) MDS is a distinct subtype.
Isolated inherited dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular enlargement and reduced systolic function.
Delayed atrioventricular conduction is a cardiac conduction disorder.
Developmental and epileptic brain disease; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic. Nystagmus and ptosis do not establish intrinsic ocular injury; sleep apnea is separately diagnosed.
Thyroid nodular disease is common, reaching ~75% of women and 17% of men by age 40. Lung and renal tumor risks alone do not establish existing organ damage.
Dopamine transport dysfunction causes infantile parkinsonism-dystonia; ocular flutter is a neurologic movement abnormality, not intrinsic eye damage.
Primary T-lymphocyte deficiency/dysfunction with lymphopenia in severe forms; recurrent pneumonia and otitis are separate infections, without established chronic lung or ear injury.
Renal tubular disease; neurologic abnormalities in 3/5, syndromic pancreatitis in 2/5 and sensorineural hearing loss in 2/5. Hypertension is secondary to renal disease.
